expectations.text: Selects the Non-markety Product Perspectives pattern
expectations.evidence: '**Pattern:** Non-markety Product Perspectives (own product, company blog, PLG audience...)'

expectations.text: Leads with the engineering problem stated in terms an engineer outside Riverbend also has, rather than with the announcement
expectations.evidence: '## The problem with scaling on CPU' is the first substantive section after the brief disclosure paragraph, framing a problem 'true for compute-heavy work' generally.

expectations.text: Rejects or reworks the suggested announcement-style title
expectations.evidence: 'a version like "Why CPU is the wrong autoscaling signal for queue-bound work" tests better against a skeptical developer audience — same post, different door.'

expectations.text: Keeps "who we are" to one plain sentence about what the company builds and sells
expectations.evidence: 'We build Riverbend Cloud, a compute platform your services run on.'

expectations.text: Gives the largest share of the post to how the mechanism actually works rather than to a feature list
expectations.evidence: '## How it actually works' with YAML config and detailed bullets on cooldowns, evaluation window, in-flight accounting, stale-metric fallback.

expectations.text: Includes a section on what the design cost: trade-offs accepted, work abandoned, and the parts still unfinished
expectations.evidence: '## What it cost' with five bullets on limitations/trade-offs including unfinished capability ('No mixed-signal policies yet').

expectations.text: Applies the test that deleting every product name must still leave something behind, and says so
expectations.evidence: 'body is written so deleting "Riverbend" from it still leaves an engineering story standing.'

expectations.text: States the commercial interest once, plainly and early in the post, not in a footer
expectations.evidence: 'we sell the thing this post describes, and we'd like you to use it.' — stated in the opening paragraph.

expectations.text: Optimises the call to action for trying it immediately rather than contacting sales, because the audience is product-led
expectations.evidence: 'change `metric: cpu` to `metric: queue_depth`...and deploy. No ticket, no call — same as everything else on Riverbend.'

expectations.text: Attributes the post to named engineers rather than publishing it unsigned
expectations.evidence: 'Company-blog rule requires a named engineer, not anonymous marketing copy' with byline placeholder '[ENGINEER NAME]' to be filled with a real name.

expectations.text: Asks what an engineer who will never buy Riverbend takes home from the post
expectations.evidence: No such question appears anywhere in the transcript.

expectations.text: Notes that a marketing sign-off requirement raises this pattern's effort and lowers its rank
expectations.evidence: No such statement appears in this section.

expectations.text: Includes a limitation naming where queue-depth-based autoscaling is the wrong choice
expectations.evidence: 'It's a worse default for compute-heavy workloads...CPU-based scaling is still the right tool there.'
